programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing ‘s Sula a’ cur seachad latha breagha foghair a’ cruinneachadh cnothan-daraich ach, ged a tha e a trusadh gu leòr, chan eil an stòras aig Bing idir a fàs! Ge-tà, tha beachd aig Flop ciamar a gheibh iad freagairt son ceist mhòr nan cnò… It’s a beautiful autumn day and Bing and Sula are busy gathering acorns. But no matter how many Bing finds, his collection gets smaller rather than bigger! However, Flop has an idea how to solve the mystery of the disappearing nuts.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing a’ lorg na brògan a bh’ aige nuair a bha e na bhèibidh, brògan beaga gliongach a tha nis ro bheag dha. Ge-tà, ‘s ann a tha na brògan freagarrach do Charlie… ach an aontaich Bing an toirt dha? Bing finds the shoes he had when he was a baby, little jingle shoes that are now much too small for him. The shoes are a perfect fit for Charlie, but is Bing willing to part with them?

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha na h-Abadas a' gabhail picnic air an dùthaich ach tha Ben airson 's gun tig iad air toir trèana-smùid. Tha Seren den bheachd gun tig aice-se air an trèan a' lorg 's i comasach air siubhal gu luath. When the Abadas have a picnic in the countryside, Ben sends them to look for a steam train. Seren decides that she will be able to find the train as she is able to travel quickly.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha camara aig Àtaidh. Tha aig a h-uile duine ri rudeigin spòrsail a dhèanamh. Chan fhada gus a bheil Nìp a’ faighinn cothrom cuideachd agus tha na dealbhan aigeasan uabhasach sònraichte. Abney's got a camera and everybody does something fun with it! Soon, Neep gets a go too, and his photos are very special.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha taisbeanadh ‘Dìneasària’ a’ gealltainn gu bheil dìneasaran air ais air talamh! Tha Peicein is a charaidean ag ionnsachadh gun e breug a tha seo, ach tha Mamaidh Pheicein fhathast dhen bheachd gu bheil na dìneasaran fìor, mar sin chan eil a’ chlann a’ leigeil guth orra. The Dinomania expo promises that dinosaurs are back on Earth. Petit and his friends discover the lie, but prefer to maintain Petit’s mum’s fantasy and do not tell her what they discovered.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ leughadh Cùm Rithe Hò Rò. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Sally Anne Garland, agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Màiri NicCumhais. Coinneach Rankin reads Cùm Rithe Hò Rò, written and illustrated by Sally Anne Garland and translated into Gaelic by Mairi MacCuish.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Troig a’ cur sìos air seinn nan càraidean, tha ’ad ’son sluagh a lorg a tha a' dol a chur luach air na tàlantan aca. Ge-tà, ’s e na Bògaisean an luchd-èisteachd a tha ro thoilichte èisteachd riutha ach ciamar a thèid leotha? When Troig is mean about the twins’ singing, they decide to go in search of folk who will appreciate their talents. However, their captive audience turns out to be Bògaisean, but how will things work out for them?

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Chan eil an latha aig Bonns a’ dol ro mhath oir tha i air i fhèin a shìneadh uiread ‘s gu bheil i air “spangachadh”. Tha i ag ionnsachadh, ge-tà, gun urrainn dhi a bhith taiceil ri a caraidean – fiù ‘s ged a tha i air i fhèin a “spangachadh”. Bonns’s day hasn’t gone too well as she has stretched so far that she has 'spanged' herself. At the end of the day, however, she learns that she can still be helpful to her friends.

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an tuathanach air a' chiad duais a ghlèidheadh agus chan urrainn dha an naidheachd a chreidsinn! Feumaidh e an tiocaid a chumail sàbhailte gu madainn is tha sin an urra ri Bitzer. Gu mi-fhortanach chan e Bitzer an cù ceart airson na h-obrach seo! An dùil an lorg e an tiocaid no na chaill e fortan an tuathanaich? The farmer can't believe his luck - he has a winning ticket! He just needs to keep it safe until morning and there's only one dog for the job! Unfortunately, Bitzer is a hopeless guard dog. Can he rescue the winning ticket, or has he lost the farmer's fortune?

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha e tighinn am follais gur e ionnsramaid-chiùil a th’ ann am bodhaig Phòil agus thathar ag iarraidh air àite fear de bhuill a’ chòmhlain as fheàrr leis, Na Coin Chaola, a ghabhail. Dave discovers that his body is a musical instrument and is asked to replace a band member in his favourite group, The Whippets.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Thathar a’ dèanamh deiseil airson cuirm-chluich bhliadhnail a’ bhaile, is tha Anna ag iarraidh pàirt na bana-phrionnsa. Ach ’s ann a tha pàirtean nam bana-bhuidseach air a thoirt dhi fhèin, Pòl agus Granaidh, is tha iad a’ feuchainn ri shealltainn gun urrainn crìoch shona a bhith aig sgeulachd nam bana-bhuidseach cuideachd. Grimsby is putting on its annual community play and Anna wants the role of princess. Cast as a witch instead, the Spuds set out to prove that witches can have happy endings, too.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Aithris bho 2016 le Angela NicIlleathain, le agallamhan le daoine a chur seachad bliadhnaichean ann am prìosan ainmeil nan Stàitean Aonaichte ann am Bàgh Ghuantanamo fo amharras ceannairc. Angela Maclean’s award-winning 2016 report, featuring exclusive interviews with former detainees at the notorious US prison at Guantanamo Bay.

programme.title: Geamaichean a' Cho-fhlaitheis Glaschu 2026/Commonwealth Games Glasgow 2026
programme.desc: Craoladh beò bho Cuirm Fosglaidh Geamaichean a’ Cho-fhlaitheis ann an Glaschu. Live coverage of the opening ceremony of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

programme.title: Na Sgiobairean mu Dheireadh/The Last Captains
programme.desc: Tha seusan a’ ghiomaich a’ tòiseachadh le brag air na h-eileanan – gun chuòta, gun tròcair. Tha gach soitheach na dhian-ruith gus an tuarastal a tha deatamach a chosnadh. Lobster season explodes on the Maggies - no quotas, no mercy. It’s a rat race on the water, with every trap chasing a make-or-break payday. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc: Anns an treas phrògram, tha Kate a’ tadhal air Rubha an Dùnain ann an cuideachd Choinnich MhicIlleathain is ag ionnsachadh beagan mu eachdraidh nan Lochlannach, tha i cuideachd a’ coinneachadh ris a’ phìobaire, Decker Forrest, a tha ag innse dhi mu phìobairean ainmeil MhicCruimein. Tha i a’ faighinn cothrom snàmh agus còcaireachd a dhèanamh còmhla ri Clare Coghill, tè a tha a’ cosnadh cliù mar shàr chòcaire. Agus bidh i cuideachd a’ tadhal air àiteachan a tha gu math ainmeil san Eilean Sgitheanach, nam measg, taigh-solais Rubha na h-Eist, Bàgh Thalasgair agus na h-Eileanan Ascrib. Kate visits Rubha an Dùnain in the company of Coinneach Maclean, where she learns a little about Viking history. She also meets piper Decker Forrest, who tells her about the famous MacCrimmon pipers. Kate gets an opportunity to swim and cook with Clare Coghill, who is making a name for herself as an expert chef. She also visits famous Skye landmarks Neist Point, Talisker Bay and the Ascrib Islands. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rudan Beaga Bòidheach/Life’s Little Things
programme.desc: Tha Niamh NicFhionghain a’ coinneachadh daoine òga eile gus rudan beaga fheuchainn a tha a’ toirt toileachas dhaibh. Bho Iòga air mullach cnoc, a bhith a’ sgrìobhadh bàrdachd, gu furachas, dòigh-beatha a’ bhana-campachaidh no a bhith a’ cluich camanachd – tha tòrr ann air an urrainn dhut a bhith taingeil an uair a tha thu air a’ bhlàr a-muigh. Skye digital creator Niamh Mackinnon meets other young people to try out the different little activities that spark joy for them. From hilltop yoga, or writing poems, to mindfulness, camper van life or playing shinty - there’s so much to appreciate when you just get out there. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: Abair gu bheil treat air leth aig Abigail – Tost Frangach. An dearbh bhiadh airson brunch le càirdean is caraidean. Abigail has a special treat in store in the form of a tasty french toast snack. It's perfect for that table brunch spread when friends and family visit. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: The Magic of Mushrooms
programme.desc: Professor Richard Fortey delves into the fascinating and normally hidden kingdom of fungi. From their spectacular birth, through a secretive underground life to their final explosive death, Richard reveals a remarkable world that few of us understand or even realise exists - yet all life on earth depends on it. In a specially built mushroom lab, with the help of mycologist Dr Patrick Hickey and some state-of-the-art technology, Richard brings to life the secret world of mushrooms as never seen before and reveals the spectacular abilities of fungi to break down waste and sustain new plant life, keeping our planet alive. Beyond the lab, Richard travels across Britain and beyond to show us the biggest, fastest and most deadly organisms on the planet - all of them fungi. He reveals their almost magical powers that have world-changing potential - opening up new frontiers in science, medicine and technology.

programme.title: Walking With...
programme.desc: Famous for waking up the nation on Radio One and his afternoon drive-time show, DJ and presenter Nick Grimshaw heads to the north east of England for a stroll through a fascinating landscape. Exploring historic areas of Warkworth and Amble in Northumberland, Nick begins his walk at first light, dipping his toes in the sea for a refreshing wake-me-up along the beach. Crossing sand dunes and an ancient river, Nick heads for the streets of Warkworth and reflects on the importance of family life, including the positive influence of his late father. Nick talks about recognising his sexuality as he was growing up - including questioning what ‘being gay’ would actually mean. Taking the short boat crossing to the extraordinary Warkworth Hermitage - a retreat carved from a sandstone cliff - Nick talks about the benefits meditation has brought to his life. As Nick approaches the end of his walk, the conversation turns to the future. He talks passionately about his desire to start his own family with his partner. Revitalised after his seven-mile walk, Nick enjoys the sunset at Amble pier and vows to return to Northumberland.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his postwar Scottish railway adventure, this time from Glasgow to the capital, Edinburgh. At Pollok Country Park in Glasgow, Michael joins a women’s running club, the Bellahouston Harriers, for a warm-up session. In parkland above the pits en route to Cuningar Loop, he finds Glasgow’s geoenergy observatory, where the British Geological Society is researching how mine water heated naturally underground can be harnessed to save energy. At Livingston North, Michael investigates a puzzling incident in 1979 in Dechmont Woods. And at Edinburgh’s famous 12th-century castle, he discovers the origins of a spectacle that has attracted tourists from far and wide since 1950, the Edinburgh Tattoo.

programme.title: This is BBC Four
programme.desc: Programmes start at 7.00pm.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: At the former Midlothian mining village of Newtongrange, Michael meets the son of a miner whose name loomed large in the disputes of the 1970s and 1980s, 'Red' Mick McGahey. On the outskirts of Edinburgh, at a recording studio in South Gyle, Michael is transported back to the wild world of 1970s pop with Bay City Rollers guitarist Stuart 'Woody' Wood. Michael leaves Edinburgh and takes the train north to Dalmeny for Queensferry, on the banks of the Firth of Forth. At the Progress Rail foundry, he marvels at the traditional skills still required to produce complex sets of rails for modern tracks in Britain and across the world. On the south bank of the Firth of Forth, Michael recalls the construction during the 1950s and 1960s of the Forth Road Bridge, which he saw as a child from the train window while crossing the rail bridge.

programme.title: Walking With...
programme.desc: Comedian and author Shappi Khorsandi walks through stunning scenery in the Peak District and along the Monsal Trail. From the hills above Tideswell, Shappi follows tracks and footpaths along Tideswell Dale and Miller’s Dale before reaching the disused railway line of the Monsal Trail. Along the way she meets residents who are charmed by her characteristic wit and ease. Taking time to appreciate the hills and ridges surrounding her, Shappi enjoys a sense of calm and composure in the country air. Walking along the trail as it tunnels through hillsides and over gorges, Shappi takes the opportunity to ‘allow the hills to hold’ her. She talks candidly about her outlook on life and love. Funny and poignant, the comedian speaks of relationships, motherhood and mental health with a refreshing honesty.

programme.title: Jesus Christ Superstar
programme.desc: A novel take on the last seven days of Jesus Christ's life, based on Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber's famous rock opera. A group of young people arrive in the Holy Land by bus to act out events leading to the Crucifixion in a blend of biblical and contemporary themes. To Judas Iscariot, Christ is a badly managed superstar, bound to lose the support of a fickle public. To the priests, he is a menace, and to Mary Magdalene, he brings a love she has never known before. Photographed against dramatic scenery in Israel, the film is performed without dialogue and includes the hit songs I Don't Know How to Love Him, Superstar and King Herod's Song.

programme.title: Norman Jewison: Hollywood Veteran
programme.desc: Tim Sebastian talks to director and producer Norman Jewison, whose acclaimed films include In the Heat of the Night, Fiddler on the Roof and Moonstruck.

programme.title: In the Heat of the Night
programme.desc: Oscar-winning thriller about a bigoted sheriff in a small Mississippi cotton town who finds himself forced into working with a black homicide expert from Philadelphia.

programme.title: Scene by Scene
programme.desc: Rod Steiger talks to Mark Cousins about his celebrated roles in On the Waterfront, Dr Zhivago and In the Heat of the Night, and shares anecdotes about James Dean, Marilyn Monroe and Elizabeth Taylor.

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Sam Willis looks at the history of the castle from its first appearance with the Normans in 1066 to the longest siege on English soil at Kenilworth Castle 200 years later. The castle arrived as an instrument of invasion but soon became a weapon with which unruly barons challenged the Crown. Tintagel Castle, the place where King Arthur is said to have been conceived, is also on the itinerary. It remains one of the most evocative of castles to this day, drawing visitors from around the world with its tales of myth and legend.

programme.desc: Rod Steiger talks to Mark Cousins about his celebrated roles in On the Waterfront, Dr Zhivago and In the Heat of the Night, and shares anecdotes about James Dean, Marilyn Monroe and Elizabeth Taylor.

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Sam Willis looks at the history of the castle from its first appearance with the Normans in 1066 to the longest siege on English soil at Kenilworth Castle 200 years later. The castle arrived as an instrument of invasion but soon became a weapon with which unruly barons challenged the Crown. Tintagel Castle, the place where King Arthur is said to have been conceived, is also on the itinerary. It remains one of the most evocative of castles to this day, drawing visitors from around the world with its tales of myth and legend.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI can write, code, plan and problem-solve in seconds. But as we hand more tasks over to machines, what happens to our own skills? In this episode, AI Decoded investigates whether AI is enhancing human intelligence or quietly eroding it. From doctors and software engineers to students growing up with AI tutors, we explore new research suggesting that reliance on AI could affect critical thinking, expertise and decision-making. Joining Marc are leading paediatric neurosurgeon Owase Jeelani, digital transformation researcher Dr Tapani Rinta-Kahila and AI Decoded co-host Dr Stephanie Hare.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's an emotional time in Wolf Wood as beloved male wolf Terry falls seriously ill. Faced with a heartbreaking decision, the keepers say goodbye to him, leaving his mate Meg alone just as she may be carrying his pups. Days later, when Meg disappears into her den and refuses to emerge, fears grow for her safety and the future of Terry's legacy. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at one of the park's most memorable stories, the ingenious homemade wheel that transformed the life of three-legged tortoise Winky and captured the hearts of viewers. Elsewhere, Kate catches up with the park's new hippos as they continue settling into their purpose-built home, while Megan puts some of the park's longest tongues to the test and joins the rhino keepers for an up-close health check.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: Two young women are shot dead while out celebrating New Year’s Eve in Birmingham. The crime bears all the hallmarks of a gangland shooting, but neither woman has any connection to the gangs. They are innocent victims, and it makes police all the more determined to catch their killers. They launch an audacious undercover operation to infiltrate rival gangs, but will they find the moment of proof they need to arrest the killer? And a thief is caught on camera stealing from a Royal Mail van in broad daylight. Despite the footage, police struggle to identify him... until a police community service officer from a neighbouring force recognises the person in the images.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A forensic biologist works tirelessly to match DNA to the killer of Julia James, and an entomologist links a killer to a double murder.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A trip down memory lane for Martin in Hampshire results in a whimsical tale about 'half a house'. In Kent, Jacqui sees a property that could be resurrected into an HMO. And Dion returns to a Stafford site with great potential that he first saw in 2023.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Myth and mystery surround this episode of the show with Charlie Ross. At the Museum of Gloucester, Charlie learns about artefacts found in the grave of a high-status woman from the late Iron Age or early Roman period. Discovered by quarrymen in the Birdlip area of Gloucestershire in 1879, the items include an ornate bowl, beads from a necklace and a world-famous bronze mirror. Further north, in Powys, two teams of bargain hunters scour the stalls of an antiques fair in Builth Wells. They are mum-and-daughter duos Babs and Rachel and Laurel and Georgina. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds – guided by expert Kate Bliss – spot a Victorian caddy, but they decide it’s not their cup of tea. The blues, meanwhile, take a fancy to a wooden foo dog but dismiss it when they see how pricey the ‘pooch’ is. With speedy Tim Weeks as their expert, the blue team finish their shop first and pass the time by having a walking race. You’ll have to watch to see who wins.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: Police are on the hunt for lawbreakers inside an ecological nature reserve, we go underwater with the scuba-diving unit, and officers break up a neighbourhood dispute.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Australia
programme.desc: Rick Stein’s journey around New South Wales takes him from the country’s interior to the Sapphire Coast.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In north Wales, Jules Hudson helps an adventurous buyer turn a favourite holiday destination into his forever home by finding a dog-friendly house with countryside walks on the doorstep. Jules also does his bit for ‘citizen science’ when he heads to the coast to learn how the public can safely monitor and protect the region’s seal population.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Michael's life took an unexpected turn when his wife Jan started losing her sight due to a rare eye condition. As they adjusted to their new reality, they decided to downsize to a more accessible home. However, Michael's prized antique collection posed a significant problem – their new home lacked the space to accommodate it all. As a temporary measure, much of the collection ended up in the home of Jan's son, but now his loft and garage are full. Michael has decided the time has come to part with the items he has taken decades to collect, so he has called in the Travelling Auctioneers to help. After a tough few years, the family would love a holiday – but how much will the funds made at auction contribute towards getting them onto a cruise ship? Auctioneer JB has just a day to uncover the items worthy of taking to auction, while restorer Lauren must restore worn pieces so they’re ready to go under the hammer. JB is convinced that a milliner's hat block with ties to the region's history will attract high bids, as well as a selection of music-themed lots. Lauren gives sympathetic restoration to a unique chair and revives an old artist's easel.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Gyles Brandreth. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: BBC News at Six
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Channel Islands News
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for the Channel Islands.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Jamie McGregor and the passionate community helping to revive Scotland’s ancient tradition of stone lifting. Once used as a test of strength, stone lifting is being reimagined for modern Scotland. Open to everyone – women and men, seasoned athletes and complete beginners alike – it has become a small but fiercely supportive community. The challenge is physical, but the reward is deeply emotional. One of the country’s most experienced stone lifters, Jamie is a prison officer, former Strongman competitor and tireless advocate for the sport. During a packed few months, he heads out on stone-lifting tours through Perthshire and Iceland, places a new lifting stone on an ancient Highland coffin road, celebrates his 50th birthday, and prepares to marry his fiancee Gail – affectionately known as his 'stone wife' – who has supported him throughout his stone-lifting journey. Along the way, we meet the fun and colourful characters who make up this close-knit 'stone family'. A warm and uplifting portrait of strength, community and heritage, this documentary explores how an ancient test of power is finding new life in the modern world.

programme.title: Alan Carr's Picture Slam
programme.desc: Comedian Alan Carr returns to host the fun and frantic quiz show where every question is a picture and every picture is worth cash. They could be anything from famous faces, places, products or logos, and teams need to name them all for a Picture Slam. Playing this time are friends Selin and Harin from London, cousins Gerard and Jeremy from South Wales and Kev and Bex, a couple from Motherwell. programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Jamie McGregor and the passionate community helping to revive Scotland’s ancient tradition of stone lifting. Once used as a test of strength, stone lifting is being reimagined for modern Scotland. Open to everyone – women and men, seasoned athletes and complete beginners alike – it has become a small but fiercely supportive community. The challenge is physical, but the reward is deeply emotional. One of the country’s most experienced stone lifters, Jamie is a prison officer, former Strongman competitor and tireless advocate for the sport. During a packed few months, he heads out on stone-lifting tours through Perthshire and Iceland, places a new lifting stone on an ancient Highland coffin road, celebrates his 50th birthday, and prepares to marry his fiancee Gail – affectionately known as his 'stone wife' – who has supported him throughout his stone-lifting journey. Along the way, we meet the fun and colourful characters who make up this close-knit 'stone family'. A warm and uplifting portrait of strength, community and heritage, this documentary explores how an ancient test of power is finding new life in the modern world.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's an emotional time in Wolf Wood as beloved male wolf Terry falls seriously ill. Faced with a heartbreaking decision, the keepers say goodbye to him, leaving his mate Meg alone just as she may be carrying his pups. Days later, when Meg disappears into her den and refuses to emerge, fears grow for her safety and the future of Terry's legacy. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at one of the park's most memorable stories, the ingenious homemade wheel that transformed the life of three-legged tortoise Winky and captured the hearts of viewers. Elsewhere, Kate catches up with the park's new hippos as they continue settling into their purpose-built home, while Megan puts some of the park's longest tongues to the test and joins the rhino keepers for an up-close health check.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: Two young women are shot dead while out celebrating New Year’s Eve in Birmingham. The crime bears all the hallmarks of a gangland shooting, but neither woman has any connection to the gangs. They are innocent victims, and it makes police all the more determined to catch their killers. They launch an audacious undercover operation to infiltrate rival gangs, but will they find the moment of proof they need to arrest the killer? And a thief is caught on camera stealing from a Royal Mail van in broad daylight. Despite the footage, police struggle to identify him... until a police community service officer from a neighbouring force recognises the person in the images.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Myth and mystery surround this episode of the show with Charlie Ross. programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Michael's life took an unexpected turn when his wife Jan started losing her sight due to a rare eye condition. As they adjusted to their new reality, they decided to downsize to a more accessible home. However, Michael's prized antique collection posed a significant problem – their new home lacked the space to accommodate it all. Michael has decided the time has come to part with the items he has taken decades to collect, so he has called in the Travelling Auctioneers to help. After a tough few years, the family would love a holiday – but how much will the funds made at auction contribute towards getting them onto a cruise ship? Auctioneer JB has just a day to uncover the items worthy of taking to auction, while restorer Lauren must restore worn pieces so they’re ready to go under the hammer. JB is convinced that a milliner's hat block with ties to the region's history will attract high bids, as well as a selection of music-themed lots. Lauren gives sympathetic restoration to a unique chair and revives an old artist's easel.

programme.title: Our Lives

Along the way, we meet the fun and colourful characters who make up this close-knit 'stone family'. A warm and uplifting portrait of strength, community and heritage, this documentary explores how an ancient test of power is finding new life in the modern world.

programme.title: Animal Park

Faced with a heartbreaking decision, the keepers say goodbye to him, leaving his mate Meg alone just as she may be carrying his pups. Days later, when Meg disappears into her den and refuses to emerge, fears grow for her safety and the future of Terry's legacy. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at one of the park's most memorable stories, the ingenious homemade wheel that transformed the life of three-legged tortoise Winky and captured the hearts of viewers. Elsewhere, Kate catches up with the park's new hippos as they continue settling into their purpose-built home, while Megan puts some of the park's longest tongues to the test and joins the rhino keepers for an up-close health check.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: Two young women are shot dead while out celebrating New Year’s Eve in Birmingham. The crime bears all the hallmarks of a gangland shooting, but neither woman has any connection to the gangs. They are innocent victims, and it makes police all the more determined to catch their killers. They launch an audacious undercover operation to infiltrate rival gangs, but will they find the moment of proof they need to arrest the killer? And a thief is caught on camera stealing from a Royal Mail van in broad daylight. Despite the footage, police struggle to identify him... until a police community service officer from a neighbouring force recognises the person in the images.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A forensic biologist works tirelessly to match DNA to the killer of Julia James, and an entomologist links a killer to a double murder.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Myth and mystery surround this episode of the show with Charlie Ross. At the Museum of Gloucester, Charlie learns about artefacts found in the grave of a high-status woman from the late Iron Age or early Roman period. Discovered by quarrymen in the Birdlip area of Gloucestershire in 1879, the items include an ornate bowl, beads from a necklace and a world-famous bronze mirror. Further north, in Powys, two teams of bargain hunters scour the stalls of an antiques fair in Builth Wells. They are mum-and-daughter duos Babs and Rachel and Laurel and Georgina. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds – guided by expert Kate Bliss – spot a Victorian caddy, but they decide it’s not their cup of tea. The blues, meanwhile, take a fancy to a wooden foo dog but dismiss it when they see how pricey the ‘pooch’ is. With speedy Tim Weeks as their expert, the blue team finish their shop first and pass the time by having a walking race. You’ll have to watch to see who wins.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Michael's life took an unexpected turn when his wife Jan started losing her sight due to a rare eye condition. As they adjusted to their new reality, they decided to downsize to a more accessible home. However, Michael's prized antique collection posed a significant problem – their new home lacked the space to accommodate it all. As a temporary measure, much of the collection ended up in the home of Jan's son, but now his loft and garage are full. Michael has decided the time has come to part with the items he has taken decades to collect, so he has called in the Travelling Auctioneers to help. After a tough few years, the family would love a holiday – but how much will the funds made at auction contribute towards getting them onto a cruise ship? Auctioneer JB has just a day to uncover the items worthy of taking to auction, while restorer Lauren must restore worn pieces so they’re ready to go under the hammer. programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Myth and mystery surround this episode of the show with Charlie Ross. programme.title: Breakfast

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's an emotional time in Wolf Wood as beloved male wolf Terry falls seriously ill. Faced with a heartbreaking decision, the keepers say goodbye to him, leaving his mate Meg alone just as she may be carrying his pups. Days later, when Meg disappears into her den and refuses to emerge, fears grow for her safety and the future of Terry's legacy. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at one of the park's most memorable stories, the ingenious homemade wheel that transformed the life of three-legged tortoise Winky and captured the hearts of viewers. Elsewhere, Kate catches up with the park's new hippos as they continue settling into their purpose-built home, while Megan puts some of the park's longest tongues to the test and joins the rhino keepers for an up-close health check.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: Two young women are shot dead while out celebrating New Year’s Eve in Birmingham. The crime bears all the hallmarks of a gangland shooting, but neither woman has any connection to the gangs. They are innocent victims, and it makes police all the more determined to catch their killers. They launch an audacious undercover operation to infiltrate rival gangs, but will they find the moment of proof they need to arrest the killer? And a thief is caught on camera stealing from a Royal Mail van in broad daylight. Despite the footage, police struggle to identify him... until a police community service officer from a neighbouring force recognises the person in the images.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A forensic biologist works tirelessly to match DNA to the killer of Julia James, and an entomologist links a killer to a double murder.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Myth and mystery surround this episode of the show with Charlie Ross. At the Museum of Gloucester, Charlie learns about artefacts found in the grave of a high-status woman from the late Iron Age or early Roman period. Discovered by quarrymen in the Birdlip area of Gloucestershire in 1879, the items include an ornate bowl, beads from a necklace and a world-famous bronze mirror. Further north, in Powys, two teams of bargain hunters scour the stalls of an antiques fair in Builth Wells. They are mum-and-daughter duos Babs and Rachel and Laurel and Georgina. The blues, meanwhile, take a fancy to a wooden foo dog but dismiss it when they see how pricey the ‘pooch’ is. programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Michael's life took an unexpected turn when his wife Jan started losing her sight due to a rare eye condition. As they adjusted to their new reality, they decided to downsize to a more accessible home. However, Michael's prized antique collection posed a significant problem – their new home lacked the space to accommodate it all. As a temporary measure, much of the collection ended up in the home of Jan's son, but now his loft and garage are full. Michael has decided the time has come to part with the items he has taken decades to collect, so he has called in the Travelling Auctioneers to help. After a tough few years, the family would love a holiday – but how much will the funds made at auction contribute towards getting them onto a cruise ship? Auctioneer JB has just a day to uncover the items worthy of taking to auction, while restorer Lauren must restore worn pieces so they’re ready to go under the hammer. JB is convinced that a milliner's hat block with ties to the region's history will attract high bids, as well as a selection of music-themed lots. Lauren gives sympathetic restoration to a unique chair and revives an old artist's easel.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Jamie McGregor and the passionate community helping to revive Scotland’s ancient tradition of stone lifting. Once used as a test of strength, stone lifting is being reimagined for modern Scotland. Open to everyone – women and men, seasoned athletes and complete beginners alike – it has become a small but fiercely supportive community. The challenge is physical, but the reward is deeply emotional. One of the country’s most experienced stone lifters, Jamie is a prison officer, former Strongman competitor and tireless advocate for the sport. During a packed few months, he heads out on stone-lifting tours through Perthshire and Iceland, places a new lifting stone on an ancient Highland coffin road, celebrates his 50th birthday, and prepares to marry his fiancee Gail – affectionately known as his 'stone wife' – who has supported him throughout his stone-lifting journey. Along the way, we meet the fun and colourful characters who make up this close-knit 'stone family'. A warm and uplifting portrait of strength, community and heritage, this documentary explores how an ancient test of power is finding new life in the modern world.

programme.title: Wales' Home of the Year
programme.desc: It’s the Grand Final! It’s now down to the final five homes – the winners of each regional episode – to go head-to-head. But only one of them can be the winner of the prestigious title. However, Michael's prized antique collection posed a significant problem – their new home lacked the space to accommodate it all. As a temporary measure, much of the collection ended up in the home of Jan's son, but now his loft and garage are full. Michael has decided the time has come to part with the items he has taken decades to collect, so he has called in the Travelling Auctioneers to help. After a tough few years, the family would love a holiday – but how much will the funds made at auction contribute towards getting them onto a cruise ship? Auctioneer JB has just a day to uncover the items worthy of taking to auction, while restorer Lauren must restore worn pieces so they’re ready to go under the hammer. JB is convinced that a milliner's hat block with ties to the region's history will attract high bids, as well as a selection of music-themed lots. Lauren gives sympathetic restoration to a unique chair and revives an old artist's easel.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Gyles Brandreth. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Jamie McGregor and the passionate community helping to revive Scotland’s ancient tradition of stone lifting. Once used as a test of strength, stone lifting is being reimagined for modern Scotland. Open to everyone – women and men, seasoned athletes and complete beginners alike – it has become a small but fiercely supportive community. The challenge is physical, but the reward is deeply emotional. One of the country’s most experienced stone lifters, Jamie is a prison officer, former Strongman competitor and tireless advocate for the sport. During a packed few months, he heads out on stone-lifting tours through Perthshire and Iceland, places a new lifting stone on an ancient Highland coffin road, celebrates his 50th birthday, and prepares to marry his fiancee Gail – affectionately known as his 'stone wife' – who has supported him throughout his stone-lifting journey. Along the way, we meet the fun and colourful characters who make up this close-knit 'stone family'. A warm and uplifting portrait of strength, community and heritage, this documentary explores how an ancient test of power is finding new life in the modern world.

programme.title: Alan Carr's Picture Slam
programme.desc: Comedian Alan Carr returns to host the fun and frantic quiz show where every question is a picture and every picture is worth cash. They could be anything from famous faces, places, products or logos, and teams need to name them all for a Picture Slam. Playing this time are friends Selin and Harin from London, cousins Gerard and Jeremy from South Wales and Kev and Bex, a couple from Motherwell. They battle it out across four rounds, shouting out answers and building their banks. But only one team can make it to the final Super Slam for the chance to win £10,000.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's an emotional time in Wolf Wood as beloved male wolf Terry falls seriously ill. Faced with a heartbreaking decision, the keepers say goodbye to him, leaving his mate Meg alone just as she may be carrying his pups. Days later, when Meg disappears into her den and refuses to emerge, fears grow for her safety and the future of Terry's legacy. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at one of the park's most memorable stories, the ingenious homemade wheel that transformed the life of three-legged tortoise Winky and captured the hearts of viewers. Elsewhere, Kate catches up with the park's new hippos as they continue settling into their purpose-built home, while Megan puts some of the park's longest tongues to the test and joins the rhino keepers for an up-close health check.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: Two young women are shot dead while out celebrating New Year’s Eve in Birmingham. The crime bears all the hallmarks of a gangland shooting, but neither woman has any connection to the gangs. They are innocent victims, and it makes police all the more determined to catch their killers. They launch an audacious undercover operation to infiltrate rival gangs, but will they find the moment of proof they need to arrest the killer? And a thief is caught on camera stealing from a Royal Mail van in broad daylight. Despite the footage, police struggle to identify him... until a police community service officer from a neighbouring force recognises the person in the images.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A forensic biologist works tirelessly to match DNA to the killer of Julia James, and an entomologist links a killer to a double murder.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A trip down memory lane for Martin in Hampshire results in a whimsical tale about 'half a house'. In Kent, Jacqui sees a property that could be resurrected into an HMO. And Dion returns to a Stafford site with great potential that he first saw in 2023.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Myth and mystery surround this episode of the show with Charlie Ross. At the Museum of Gloucester, Charlie learns about artefacts found in the grave of a high-status woman from the late Iron Age or early Roman period. Discovered by quarrymen in the Birdlip area of Gloucestershire in 1879, the items include an ornate bowl, beads from a necklace and a world-famous bronze mirror. Further north, in Powys, two teams of bargain hunters scour the stalls of an antiques fair in Builth Wells. They are mum-and-daughter duos Babs and Rachel and Laurel and Georgina. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds – guided by expert Kate Bliss – spot a Victorian caddy, but they decide it’s not their cup of tea. The blues, meanwhile, take a fancy to a wooden foo dog but dismiss it when they see how pricey the ‘pooch’ is. With speedy Tim Weeks as their expert, the blue team finish their shop first and pass the time by having a walking race. You’ll have to watch to see who wins.

programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's an emotional time in Wolf Wood as beloved male wolf Terry falls seriously ill. Faced with a heartbreaking decision, the keepers say goodbye to him, leaving his mate Meg alone just as she may be carrying his pups. Days later, when Meg disappears into her den and refuses to emerge, fears grow for her safety and the future of Terry's legacy. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at one of the park's most memorable stories, the ingenious homemade wheel that transformed the life of three-legged tortoise Winky and captured the hearts of viewers. Elsewhere, Kate catches up with the park's new hippos as they continue settling into their purpose-built home, while Megan puts some of the park's longest tongues to the test and joins the rhino keepers for an up-close health check.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: Two young women are shot dead while out celebrating New Year’s Eve in Birmingham. The crime bears all the hallmarks of a gangland shooting, but neither woman has any connection to the gangs. They are innocent victims, and it makes police all the more determined to catch their killers. They launch an audacious undercover operation to infiltrate rival gangs, but will they find the moment of proof they need to arrest the killer? And a thief is caught on camera stealing from a Royal Mail van in broad daylight. Despite the footage, police struggle to identify him... until a police community service officer from a neighbouring force recognises the person in the images.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A forensic biologist works tirelessly to match DNA to the killer of Julia James, and an entomologist links a killer to a double murder.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A trip down memory lane for Martin in Hampshire results in a whimsical tale about 'half a house'. In Kent, Jacqui sees a property that could be resurrected into an HMO. And Dion returns to a Stafford site with great potential that he first saw in 2023.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Myth and mystery surround this episode of the show with Charlie Ross. At the Museum of Gloucester, Charlie learns about artefacts found in the grave of a high-status woman from the late Iron Age or early Roman period. Discovered by quarrymen in the Birdlip area of Gloucestershire in 1879, the items include an ornate bowl, beads from a necklace and a world-famous bronze mirror. Further north, in Powys, two teams of bargain hunters scour the stalls of an antiques fair in Builth Wells. They are mum-and-daughter duos Babs and Rachel and Laurel and Georgina. With 60 minutes on the clock, the reds – guided by expert Kate Bliss – spot a Victorian caddy, but they decide it’s not their cup of tea. The blues, meanwhile, take a fancy to a wooden foo dog but dismiss it when they see how pricey the ‘pooch’ is. With speedy Tim Weeks as their expert, the blue team finish their shop first and pass the time by having a walking race. You’ll have to watch to see who wins.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Michael's life took an unexpected turn when his wife Jan started losing her sight due to a rare eye condition. As they adjusted to their new reality, they decided to downsize to a more accessible home. However, Michael's prized antique collection posed a significant problem – their new home lacked the space to accommodate it all. As a temporary measure, much of the collection ended up in the home of Jan's son, but now his loft and garage are full. Michael has decided the time has come to part with the items he has taken decades to collect, so he has called in the Travelling Auctioneers to help. After a tough few years, the family would love a holiday – but how much will the funds made at auction contribute towards getting them onto a cruise ship? Auctioneer JB has just a day to uncover the items worthy of taking to auction, while restorer Lauren must restore worn pieces so they’re ready to go under the hammer. JB is convinced that a milliner's hat block with ties to the region's history will attract high bids, as well as a selection of music-themed lots. Lauren gives sympathetic restoration to a unique chair and revives an old artist's easel.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Jamie McGregor and the passionate community helping to revive Scotland’s ancient tradition of stone lifting. Once used as a test of strength, stone lifting is being reimagined for modern Scotland. Open to everyone – women and men, seasoned athletes and complete beginners alike – it has become a small but fiercely supportive community. The challenge is physical, but the reward is deeply emotional. One of the country’s most experienced stone lifters, Jamie is a prison officer, former Strongman competitor and tireless advocate for the sport. During a packed few months, he heads out on stone-lifting tours through Perthshire and Iceland, places a new lifting stone on an ancient Highland coffin road, celebrates his 50th birthday, and prepares to marry his fiancee Gail – affectionately known as his 'stone wife' – who has supported him throughout his stone-lifting journey. Along the way, we meet the fun and colourful characters who make up this close-knit 'stone family'. A warm and uplifting portrait of strength, community and heritage, this documentary explores how an ancient test of power is finding new life in the modern world.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Michael's life took an unexpected turn when his wife Jan started losing her sight due to a rare eye condition. As they adjusted to their new reality, they decided to downsize to a more accessible home. However, Michael's prized antique collection posed a significant problem – their new home lacked the space to accommodate it all. As a temporary measure, much of the collection ended up in the home of Jan's son, but now his loft and garage are full. Michael has decided the time has come to part with the items he has taken decades to collect, so he has called in the Travelling Auctioneers to help. After a tough few years, the family would love a holiday – but how much will the funds made at auction contribute towards getting them onto a cruise ship? Auctioneer JB has just a day to uncover the items worthy of taking to auction, while restorer Lauren must restore worn pieces so they’re ready to go under the hammer. JB is convinced that a milliner's hat block with ties to the region's history will attract high bids, as well as a selection of music-themed lots. Lauren gives sympathetic restoration to a unique chair and revives an old artist's easel.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Gyles Brandreth. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Jamie McGregor and the passionate community helping to revive Scotland’s ancient tradition of stone lifting. Once used as a test of strength, stone lifting is being reimagined for modern Scotland. Open to everyone – women and men, seasoned athletes and complete beginners alike – it has become a small but fiercely supportive community. The challenge is physical, but the reward is deeply emotional. One of the country’s most experienced stone lifters, Jamie is a prison officer, former Strongman competitor and tireless advocate for the sport. During a packed few months, he heads out on stone-lifting tours through Perthshire and Iceland, places a new lifting stone on an ancient Highland coffin road, celebrates his 50th birthday, and prepares to marry his fiancee Gail – affectionately known as his 'stone wife' – who has supported him throughout his stone-lifting journey. Along the way, we meet the fun and colourful characters who make up this close-knit 'stone family'. A warm and uplifting portrait of strength, community and heritage, this documentary explores how an ancient test of power is finding new life in the modern world.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: Hidden Lives
programme.desc: Award-winning journalist Peter Ross experiences the pomp and pageantry of the Bo'ness Fair, said to be the largest children's fair in Europe. Each year since 1897, a local schoolgirl has been crowned Fair Queen in a ceremony which arguably means more to the town than a real coronation would to the nation. The graft and craft that goes into celebrating the occasion has to be seen to believed. It is a psychedelic trip, featuring hand-built plywood castles bigger than houses, custom-made dresses that would be the envy of any young royal, and a grand procession with bands and floats which is a sort of Scottish mardi gras.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: It's all about the borders at Beechgrove Garden as Brian Cunningham and Kirsty Wilson replant, fill gaps and replace losses all around the plot. Kirsty revisits her hot border, designed to display vibrant colours at the height of summer. The winter temperatures killed off a few plants, so she will be trying out some alternatives. Brian is in the calendar border, created to have some form of colour or interest every month of the year. It has not had much attention this year, so Brian will be topping it up to ensure year-round performance. Kirsty will also be planting in the border behind Beechgrove's main pond, where other gaps have appeared, and she is building a new structure to create a habitat for pollinators. There is a trip to visit a great garden on the Cowal Peninsula, and all the week's handy hints.

programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers and Grado uncover the best holiday escapes in Scotland. But it’s up to friends and families from all over Scotland to decide which escapes make it to the grand final. Scotland's greatest mind, body and soul escape is decided by father and daughter Graham and Aimee from Dumfriesshire. They jump out of their city break comfort zone into three well-being retreats, as they are soothed by the elegant Stobo spa, experience a close encounter at Sheepy Sleepovers and enjoy a handcrafted Romani caravan at Roulotte Retreat.

programme.title: Granite Harbour
programme.desc: A birthday celebration ends in tragedy when a girl is found dead near a traveller site. As tensions rise, Lindo and the team uncover secrets that threaten to tear a community apart.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Fighting the lawless and ensuring the law wins. Volunteer officer Ken Beattie wrestles with a dodgy dealer and the dilemma of whether that dealer is or isn't offering him a bribe. Officer Karen is in the middle of something and has no time whatsoever for whatever Bobby wants to bother her about - even if it involves a famous face recognising a community hero. Party animals go wild in the country as Charlie introduces Jane to the etiquette surrounding the rural festival known as the Butterfist. And the Chief pushes his professional productivity to the max as he receives an open razor shave at his desk. Starring Jack Docherty, James Allenby-Kirk, Karen Bartke, Darren Connell, Chris Forbes, Ashley Smith and special guest Shereen Nanjiani.

programme.title: Cumming to the Cabaret
programme.desc: Alan Cumming provides a behind-the-scenes glimpse into the eclectic group of artists at his Cabaret-themed East Village club as they navigate their personal and professional lives in today's turbulent political landscape.

programme.title: Cumming to the Cabaret
programme.desc: Cunning wows the crowd with the city's only drag king competition as Alan heads to Hollywood to receive his star on the Walk of Fame. Daphne enlists Michelle and Cunning to join her in a new show at the club.

programme.title: Des Doesn’t Do...
programme.desc: Des Clarke is scared out of his wits by fellow comedian and horror fan Robert Florence, who attempts to turnaround Des’s deep-rooted dislike of horror by deconstructing the genre. Des faces a film fright night, a peek behind the scenes at Scotland’s horror movie industry and an unforgettable ghost tour around Glamis Castle - but will Des finally overcome his inner coward?

programme.title: Loop
programme.desc: In late 2022, Leyla Josephine’s debut poetry book, In Public/In Private, was published, followed by a whirlwind tour around England, Scotland and Northern Ireland. We meet the performance poet at the top of her game as she pauses for breath in her adopted hometown of Prestwick. In an exclusive recording from Prestwick Beach, Leyla reads Questions I Have for Birds and gets ready for her much-anticipated homecoming gig at Glasgow’s iconic King Tut’s Wah Wah Hut.

programme.title: Roman Kemp: The Fight for Young Lives
programme.desc: On a daily basis, Roman Kemp is contacted by young people who are struggling. With people turning to him for advice, he’s questioning whether or not there is a worsening mental health crisis and asking if these young people should be offered more support in their own communities. This documentary follows Roman as he immerses himself in schools, youth centres and treatment settings around the country, meets with experts and charities, and visits the Houses of Parliament to try to understand the potential solutions for improving the mental health of young people in the UK today.

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: We head to sunny south London and the remarkable Rivoli Ballrooms, a world-famous venue that’s dripping in original vintage décor. Designed by Henley Attwater in 1913, it’s one of the last 1950s style ballrooms in the country. Five brand new acts take to the stage in front of a packed house of more than two hundred comedy lovers. Award-winning comedian Laura Smyth is the host, and joining her are the three judges – Mexican-born stand-up Lara Ricote, Motherland writer Holly Walsh and head judge, Babatunde Aleshe. Muhsin Yesilada, Maia Tassalini, Limahl Germain, Alfie Packham and Frankie Thompson each perform their set before the judges decide who will go through to the grand final. There can only be one winner, so who will it be?

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson celebrates the 50th birthday of the Jaguar E-type by driving a modern half-a-million pound interpretation of this classic sports car before putting on a typically low-key birthday party involving live music, classic fighter planes and a group of Royal Marines. Meanwhile, Richard Hammond is in South Africa to test a bigger, even more rugged alternative to the famous Hummer, while James May meets up with gold medal winning British Olympian Amy Williams for a wintry test of the latest Mini rally car. Plus the power crazed BMW 1 series M is on the test track and another top celebrity guest takes their place in the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve and the team are on the search for deadly animals in the steaming swamps of the southern USA. The contenders are everywhere, not least the alligators that live in just about every pond and lake. But the first animal on the list is a complete surprise, a monster fish with two rows of sharp fangs that certainly keeps Steve on his toes. The crew find themselves up to their armpits in a swamp hoping to find a deadly snake with the unusual name of cottonmouth. Last but not least, Steve and his team come face to face with an enormous record-breaking predatory turtle.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Naturalist Steve Backshall heads to the Bahamas in order to get up close and personal with a whole bunch of sharks. There are plenty of shark species to choose from and Steve has his work cut out deciding which ones are worthy of a place on his Deadly 60 list. Hooking up with shark scientists helps him decide and gives him an opportunity to release some baby sharks into the wild, and he learns how to hypnotise them with his bare hands. Getting mobbed by hungry reef sharks and swimming with a four-metre tiger shark are all in a day's work for Steve and the team!

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: It's the ultimate test of man against machine or should that be dog against machine? Either way, it's Top Gear's most ambitious and arduous challenge to date. Jeremy Clarkson, James May and Richard Hammond attempt to race from the town of Resolute in northern Canada to the Magnetic North Pole, 450 miles away. The terrain in between is some of the toughest on earth - a mix of mountainous land masses and jagged sea ice where temperatures can drop to -65C. And then there are the polar bears - the Arctic is home to 80 per cent of the world's population, and when it comes to lunch they really don't care if it's seal or human. This being Top Gear, the three presenters' modes of transport are a little out of the ordinary. Jeremy and James drive a specially adapted pickup truck, whilst Richard travels on something a little less high-tech - a sled pulled by a team of ten Canadian Inuit dogs. Pitting dog power against horse power may sound like a one-sided contest, but given the nature of the terrain, there's no telling who will make it to the Pole first. In fact, there's no guarantee that either team will reach the finish line at all.

programme.title: The Traitors Canada
programme.desc: The guests are shocked to find four players absent from the breakfast table, only to learn that their fate in the game is at the risk of being buried. While the remaining players attempt to save them from a grave fate, they quickly discover that not everyone will make it out alive.

programme.title: The Traitors Canada
programme.desc: With suspicion intensifying inside the manor and a focus on one player in particular, another sees it as an opportunity to set their cunning plan into motion and make a swift strike for revenge.

programme.title: The Traitors Canada
programme.desc: In the aftermath of an eventful Round Table and banishment, the remaining guests begin to examine the exchanges between certain players the night before, while another finds themself stranded and at the mercy of the Traitors.

programme.title: The Traitors Canada
programme.desc: With a Faithful treading troubled waters with their fellow guests, the Traitors see an opportunity to set a trap disguised as an invitation to join their midst. The Traitors wait with bated breath to see if their plan will succeed or if the player figures out their malicious intent.

programme.title: My Old Ass
programme.desc: In this coming-of-age fable, free-spirited teenager Elliott encounters her wisecracking 39-year-old future self and can’t escape her influence. On the cusp of leaving home for college, Elliott is determined to have one last summer packed with good times. To celebrate her 18th birthday, she boats off to a remote island with her best friends to trip on magic mushrooms. But just when Elliott thinks she’s not feeling a thing, she suddenly finds herself chatting with a woman who claims to be her literal 'old ass', the person she is apparently destined to become in two decades' time! Prodded for advice, Elliott’s future self gives her one major warning: avoid anyone named Chad, which sounds easy enough. But when Elliott meets the very Chad she was supposed to dodge, things get complicated. Elliott starts to open herself to what her future self might have to show her... and vice versa!

Vernon Kay keeps the quiz on track, while Traitors star Paul Gorton is back as an unreliable tour guide, turning the spotlight on Enniskillen and its surprising stories. With scores beginning to take shape, attention shifts towards who could become the week's overall champion.

programme.title: Scamanda
programme.desc: As Nancy and Detective Martinez dig deeper, the IRS steps in. Is Amanda's web of lies about to unravel?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. After years of planning, it's a landmark day as four hippos take their first steps beyond their new home and into Half Mile Pond. The keepers have spent months preparing for this moment, but once the hippos venture into the water, there's no telling what they'll do next, or whether they'll come back when called. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit the story of Kadu, one of the park's most loved Amur tigers. When a routine procedure uncovered devastating news, her keepers faced one of the hardest decisions of their careers in a story that remains one of the most emotional moments in Animal Park's history. Elsewhere, the Farmyard celebrates the arrival of adorable pygmy goat kids, while Megan McCubbin meets a critically endangered cotton-top tamarin who has recently given birth to a precious new baby, giving hope for the future of the species.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: With JB and Lauren’s help, Tanya lets go of her parents’ treasured items to fund a dream trip to India, thus honouring her father’s memory and reconnecting with her heritage.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: After the scorching heat of early summer, Monty is working to keep the garden looking its best through the season's challenges. He tackles essential jobs, including cutting back perennials to make room for more colour, tending long grass and pruning step-over apples, while proving there's still time to sow vegetables for delicious late-summer harvests. Best of all, he enjoys some of summer's greatest rewards – lifting the first new potatoes and gathering fragrant sweet peas for the house. Adam Frost discovers a remarkable 2.5-acre walled garden in Surrey packed with hidden gems and unexpected delights. Sue Kent demonstrates how imagination and resourcefulness can transform everyday items into beautiful and productive growing spaces, while in Cornwall, there's a fruit and vegetable professor whose lifelong fascination with pests and diseases is helping gardeners grow healthier crops. Plus a visit to a grower with a striking collection of crassulas, showcasing the extraordinary beauty and diversity of these popular succulents.

programme.title: BBC News

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games

A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp hosts this quiz show with sidekick Sarah Greene where contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Self-taught farming couple SJ and Nat rear their herd of free range pigs in the Pennines near Todmorden, West Yorkshire, and over the past decade have built up a farm that now supports them. They are proud of their award-winning sausages and hope their passion for high-welfare meat, and their freshly cooked samples, will attract plenty of attention at the Lancashire Game and Country Festival. As well as notching up sausage sales, SJ is keen to launch her new experimental products on the palates of passing shoppers. Meanwhile, for organic farmers Emma and Ian, who live in the Ribble Valley, it’s their first time at the festival. As well as aiming for a sell-out day for their grass-fed beef, it’s a chance for Ian to spread the word about their farm and reel in new trade. Emma focuses on her first love, the cows, and Ian is the people person. For both of these farming couples, the hard work of being at the festival will be worth it if they go home in an empty van and manage to win the hearts and loyalty of new customers.

programme.title: The Hidden World of Hospitality with Tom Kerridge
programme.desc: Tom visits three restaurants hoping to expand their businesses. Among them are a fusion restaurant combining Caribbean and west African dishes, a vegan restaurant and a pub-cum-butcher's shop.

programme.title: Wild Brazil
programme.desc: This intimate journey to the heart of a Brazil continues, following the animal families as they face the formidable monsoon rains. The giant otter babies must watch out for predatory jaguars and learn to swim before their river floods. The coatis must eat all they can before their world disappears underwater, and the youngest capuchin monkey has to learn some clever survival skills fast.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Faisal Islam.

programme.title: The Inspection
programme.desc: A young gay black man, rejected by his mother and with few options for his future, decides to join the US Marines, doing whatever it takes to succeed in a system that would cast him aside. programme.title: Ambulance

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?

With scores beginning to take shape, attention shifts towards who could become the week's overall champion.

programme.title: Scamanda
programme.desc: As Nancy and Detective Martinez dig deeper, the IRS steps in. Is Amanda's web of lies about to unravel?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. After years of planning, it's a landmark day as four hippos take their first steps beyond their new home and into Half Mile Pond. The keepers have spent months preparing for this moment, but once the hippos venture into the water, there's no telling what they'll do next, or whether they'll come back when called. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit the story of Kadu, one of the park's most loved Amur tigers. When a routine procedure uncovered devastating news, her keepers faced one of the hardest decisions of their careers in a story that remains one of the most emotional moments in Animal Park's history. Elsewhere, the Farmyard celebrates the arrival of adorable pygmy goat kids, while Megan McCubbin meets a critically endangered cotton-top tamarin who has recently given birth to a precious new baby, giving hope for the future of the species.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: With JB and Lauren’s help, Tanya lets go of her parents’ treasured items to fund a dream trip to India, thus honouring her father’s memory and reconnecting with her heritage.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. After years of planning, it's a landmark day as four hippos take their first steps beyond their new home and into Half Mile Pond. The keepers have spent months preparing for this moment, but once the hippos venture into the water, there's no telling what they'll do next, or whether they'll come back when called. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit the story of Kadu, one of the park's most loved Amur tigers. When a routine procedure uncovered devastating news, her keepers faced one of the hardest decisions of their careers in a story that remains one of the most emotional moments in Animal Park's history. Elsewhere, the Farmyard celebrates the arrival of adorable pygmy goat kids, while Megan McCubbin meets a critically endangered cotton-top tamarin who has recently given birth to a precious new baby, giving hope for the future of the species.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: After the scorching heat of early summer, Monty is working to keep the garden looking its best through the season's challenges. He tackles essential jobs, including cutting back perennials to make room for more colour, tending long grass and pruning step-over apples, while proving there's still time to sow vegetables for delicious late-summer harvests. Best of all, he enjoys some of summer's greatest rewards – lifting the first new potatoes and gathering fragrant sweet peas for the house. Adam Frost discovers a remarkable 2.5-acre walled garden in Surrey packed with hidden gems and unexpected delights. Sue Kent demonstrates how imagination and resourcefulness can transform everyday items into beautiful and productive growing spaces, while in Cornwall, there's a fruit and vegetable professor whose lifelong fascination with pests and diseases is helping gardeners grow healthier crops. Plus a visit to a grower with a striking collection of crassulas, showcasing the extraordinary beauty and diversity of these popular succulents.

programme.desc: Grizzy and the Lemmings fight for the last jar of Yummy with magic Mayan bracelets.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck and Frog must move a famous pop star’s possessions from one mansion to another. However, they are unable to do it with anything remaining in one piece.

programme.title: Submarine Jim
programme.desc: The sub is haunted by the USS Mean Shark - but what is its goal?

programme.title: Odd Squad
programme.desc: An international high-tech organisation run by kids, which investigates all things strange, weird and, most importantly, odd.

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Liko and friends train together at the Pokémon League's battle room in Paldea.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: To convince Damien of Bloom's danger, Vexius hatches a plan to force her to lose control of her powers in an attempt to rescue Mike and Vanessa.

programme.title: Go Get Arty
programme.desc: The Kwapongs make the wildest animal masks ever - but who will win? Michelle Wibowo makes Taylor Swift from old coffee, and Dame Sarah Storey draws a red panda!

programme.title: So Awkward
programme.desc: Lily adopts a new look and personality to fit in at Burke Hill University, but it gets awkward when she can’t maintain the lie with her new flatmates Frankie, Seb and Samson.

programme.title: Malory Towers
programme.desc: Darrell’s final year starts with a fierce argument with Gwen, but she knows they need to work together. Meanwhile, French student Celeste joins the Third and plays a prank on the teachers!
